subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should `openclaw status --deep` and deep JSON trust live `doctor.memory.status` provider/runtime health when local CLI memory status is null, or should current `not checked` behavior remain the supported contract?
rationale: Current main intentionally avoids some local memory probing, but the issue asks for a stronger live-gateway status signal and the open PR implements a competing contract on stale code.

options.title: Adopt live-gateway memory status
options.body: Revive or replace the open PR with a current-main implementation that exposes live provider/runtime health and adds regression coverage for external memory plugins.

options.title: Keep not-checked behavior
options.body: Declare skipped/local-null memory status as intentional, close this request, and leave broader local plugin side-effect work to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599.

recommendation.title: Adopt live-gateway memory status
recommendation.body: Revive or replace the open PR with a current-main implementation that exposes live provider/runtime health and adds regression coverage for external memory plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the recent gateway/status rewrite that now owns the behavior and is the clearest available decision owner from current history.
